title: The Indian education trap: a degree can be a career mistake
description: Compare a degree’s cost, signal, and opportunity trade-offs with your target work, existing experience, and other routes to qualification.
body:
Compare a degree’s cost, signal, and opportunity trade-offs with your target work, existing experience, and other routes to qualification.

The admission letter and the imagined life

A student in a small Indian city receives an admission offer and is asked to decide quickly. The brochure promises a respected degree, a campus, and employability. None of those words answers what the student will practise, who will teach it, what debt the family will carry, or which work the graduate can credibly seek. The practical test is narrower than the slogan. In this section, the programme must be evaluated through its actual documents, teaching, cost, and options rather than its marketing label. Ask what is observable in your own team, city, or household, and separate that observation from an interpretation. A useful answer has an owner, a document, or a repeated behaviour behind it. If the answer is only a confident anecdote, keep it as a hypothesis. That restraint matters in India, where the same job title can describe a product team in Bengaluru, a delivery team in Kochi, a family business in Jaipur, or a global shift serving a client elsewhere.
